data.title: Matt's Script Archive: The Scripts That Reshaped the Web
data.article_summary: 文章借90年代高中生Matt Wright的脚本网站说明：易用工具往往会被大量普通人采用，哪怕代码粗糙、漏洞百出。其论坛、计数器等脚本虽推动早期网络普及，却因长期缺乏维护埋下安全隐患；后续替代品也会随技术演进而过时。作者借此指出，互联网使用习惯常由“方便先于安全”塑造。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Matt’s Script Archive 的历史意义与安全问题，讨论其对早期网页开发的启蒙作用，以及是否应以今天的安全标准来评价当年的脚本生态。

不同观点：
• **怀旧与启蒙价值**：不少评论者认为这些脚本是自己进入编程/网页开发的起点。`madrox`、`arscan`、`jamiecurle`、`knadh`、`tonyoconnell` 都提到，Matt 的脚本让他们第一次接触动态网页、表单邮件、论坛或聊天功能，甚至直接改变了职业路径。`jamiecurle` 还举例说，打开 `formmail.pl` 发现是“可读的英文”而非“难懂的二进制”，极具启发性。  
• **安全糟糕但符合时代背景**：`madrox` 反对把当年的 WWWBoard 直接类比今天的“vibe coding”漏洞问题，认为早期互联网环境完全不同：没有大规模自动扫描、金融欺诈和产业化恶意软件，网站被黑更多是“涂鸦式炫技”。因此，用今天的风险框架回看当年并不公平。  
• **安全问题确实严重**：`Twirrim` 从 ISP 运维视角反驳怀旧滤镜，指出这些脚本在 2000 年代中期是“噩梦”，常被用来发垃圾邮件等，清理滥用是日常工作。`arscan` 也承认自己某种程度上是“通过照着例子做才吃到安全教训”。  
• **“能用”比“优雅”更重要**：`CM30` 进一步提炼争论核心：低质量、拼凑式、效率差的工具，仍可能因填补真实需求而广受欢迎。其模组社区例子说明，专业开发者虽然鄙视这类作品，但在缺少更好替代品时，用户会选择“虽差但可用”的方案。

补充讨论：
• `borwick` 提到 `Not Matt's Scripts` 试图以更安全的方式重写热门脚本，说明社区后来也在修补这类遗产。  
• `tgorgolione` 提议像保护历史建筑一样保存历史网站。  
• `Dwedit` 补充了 WWWBoard 可被“空格标题”恶作剧利用的具体例子。

Currently, I’m in the midst of writing
a big post about the roots of web forums, but I hit on an aside weird enough that I decided to stop writing that and work on a separate post. Because I think it actually explains a lot about the way people use the internet.
Essentially, here’s the deal. Around 1995 or so, a high schooler named
Matt Wright
decided to launch a website that shared some basic website tools that he programmed. Many of these were dead-simple, things like contact forms, guestbooks, and web counters. One in particular, WWWBoard, became a massive hit, becoming one of the first widely used web forum apps on the internet.
The copyright notice for WWWBoard, Wright’s widely used forum-hosting software.
The site Wright built,
Matt’s Script Archive
, unwittingly helped to highlight the divergence between how normal people think about software, and the developer’s perspective.
Wright, and others like him, hit upon an obvious need. Regular people found these scripts, ran them, and suddenly had forums, counters, and contact forms. They got the job done. But programmers who weren’t in high school and weren’t so wet behind the ears looked aghast at what Wright had done: He had spread poorly designed, but widely used software across the internet. This software was packed with security issues, but worst of all, it wasn’t really getting updated all that much.
How serious are the security issues? Well,
a look at OpenCVE
points out some very serious problems that range from bugs that emerged from massive exposure to some questionable design decisions. (Keeping an encrypted password file in the root? Making it possible to grab env variables via a URL? Not smart!)
One exploit in particular, affecting Wright’s textcounter tool, stands out among the list:
CVE-1999-1479
, with a score of 10.0 critical, effectively allows exploiters to execute code on the server as root.
You mean Matt has a script archive? Let’s have the Perl pros take a turn.
This state of affairs got serious enough that a competing website, called
nms
, essentially was launched to replace Matt’s buggy scripts with drop-in versions aren’t full of security exploits from bad coding. Their POV:
The problem is that the scripts in Matt’s Script Archive aren’t very good. The scripts are well known amongst the Perl community to be badly written, buggy, and insecure. Anyone asking for support on Matt’s scripts in any forum will be told in no uncertain terms that they shouldn’t use his scripts.
Unfortunately for some time there were no replacements for Matt’s scripts that you would want people to use. In 2001, the London Perl Mongers decided to address this problem and write a series of drop-in replacements for Matt’s scripts. This project is the result.
That said, you shouldn’t use nms either, because it hasn’t been updated in about 20 years. What gives? After I wrote this,
Dave Cross
, who helped develop the nms tool, reached out and noted that while he still programs in Perl, the mechanisms we use to program and host websites have sharply diverged over the past 30 years. “The best practices in Perl web development moved on from CGI a long time ago,” he wrote in an email.
On top of all that, security practices have continued to evolve.
“The internet is a very different and far less trusting place these days,” Cross added. “One of the problems with FormMail, for example, is that it could be used to send spam. That hole was fixed but, today, things like SPF and DKIM would make it very hard to deliver email to its intended recipient.”
(Even if Cross actually wanted to update the nms scripts, he would be unable to—as he doesn’t have his SourceForge login anymore, nor does he really remember how Subversion works. But we’re not exactly lacking for alternatives, either.)
TFW your old computer is at risk of getting hacked by a guestbook. (
DepositPhotos.com
)
Matt’s scripts, the easy option, and the problem with overexposure
When so many people use something that it becomes part of the internet’s lingua franca, it’s inevitable exploits are going to emerge. There’s a reason WordPress and Windows each have reputations as bug-ridden, and it’s largely because of the number of eyes on the given tools.
With that in mind, I don’t think it’s fair to blame Wright for having bad code—after all, it wasn’t like he knew it was going to become a huge platform.
(For what it’s worth, Wright himself later recommended the nms scripts instead of his own, reminding folks he wrote his original scripts as a kid. “The code you find at Matt’s Script Archive is not representative of how even I would code these days,”
he wrote on his site
. “My interests and activities have moved on, however, and I just have not found the time to update all of my scripts.”)

• **安全问题确实严重**：`Twirrim` 从 ISP 运维视角反驳怀旧滤镜，指出这些脚本在 2000 年代中期是“噩梦”，常被用来发垃圾邮件等，清理滥用是日常工作。`arscan` 也承认自己某种程度上是“通过照着例子做才吃到安全教训”。  
• **“能用”比“优雅”更重要**：`CM30` 进一步提炼争论核心：低质量、拼凑式、效率差的工具，仍可能因填补真实需求而广受欢迎。其模组社区例子说明，专业开发者虽然鄙视这类作品，但在缺少更好替代品时，用户会选择“虽差但可用”的方案。

补充讨论：
• `borwick` 提到 `Not Matt's Scripts` 试图以更安全的方式重写热门脚本，说明社区后来也在修补这类遗产。  
• `tgorgolione` 提议像保护历史建筑一样保存历史网站。  
• `Dwedit` 补充了 WWWBoard 可被“空格标题”恶作剧利用的具体例子。

data.title: What Is a Nomogram and Why Would It Interest Me?
data.author: Eridanus2
data.article_summary:
**PyNomo** 是一个用于生成**列线图（nomogram）**的Python库。

列线图是一种图形计算工具，发明于1880年，通过在多条刻度线上放置直尺，即可快速求解多变量数学公式。它曾广泛用于工程计算，在计算机普及前尤为重要。

PyNomo支持9种常见函数关系的列线图自动生成，输出PDF矢量图，用户只需提供变量函数即可。列线图至今仍应用于医学、弹道、化工、统计、水利等多个领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：诺模图（Nomogram）的价值、应用场景及相关资源

不同观点：
• **实用推荐派**：cscheid 强烈推荐学习贝叶斯定理诺模图，认为应熟练到闭眼可用；analogpixel 补充了手工制作诺模图的视频教程。

• **领域应用派**：forgotpwagain 介绍电气工程师常用的史密斯圆图（Smith Chart），指出其接受度取决于电磁学课程质量；cckolon 指出美国海军至今仍在核反应堆化学控制中使用诺模图，强调其现实延续性。

• **历史工具爱好者**：alnwlsn 推荐 Chris Staecker 的 YouTube 频道，该频道专注于计算机出现前人们使用的各类数学工具，认为这些工具兼具巧思与复杂性。

Introduction
¶
What is a Nomogram and Why Would It Interest Me?
¶
A
nomogram
or
nomograph
is a diagram that provides an easy, graphical way of calculating the result of a mathematical formula. Sometimes also called an
alignment chart
, a nomogram consists of a set of numbered scales, usually one for each variable in the formula, arranged so that a straightedge can be placed across known values to find the unknown value that solves the formula. Since an equation in two variables is usually represented by a graph, most nomograms represent formulas that involve three or more variables.
These graphical calculators were invented in 1880 by Philbert Maurice d’Ocagne and used extensively for many years to provide engineers with fast graphical calculations of complicated formulas to a practical precision. Electronic calculators and computers have made nomograms much less common today, but when a fast, handy calculator of a particular formula is needed they can be very useful. The cost to produce one is a sheet of paper, and they are fun to design, easy to use, and can be beautiful designs that engage people.
For example, here’s a nomogram from 1920 that relates the variables
\(l\)
,
\(s\)
,
\(r\)
and
\(\alpha\)
for a slider-crank mechanism:
The equation that this solves is quite complicated:
\(s = r(1 - \cos \alpha) + l(1 - (1 - \lambda^2 \sin^2 \alpha)^{1/2})\)
where
\(\lambda = r/l\)
There is a sample isopleth line on the nomogram that solves the equation for one set of values, scaled by
\(r\)
. For a value
\(\lambda = r/l = 0.35\)
and an angle
\(\alpha = 75^{\circ}\)
, we find that
\(s/2r \approx 0.455\)
, where we read off the same sides of the
\(s/2r\)
and
\(\alpha\)
scales. Note that in practice this nomogram would be drawn by a draftsman to a much larger scale for greater precision.
Try it out yourself! Pick a radius
\(r\)
, a length
\(l \geq 2r\)
and an angle
\(\alpha\)
, and find
\(s\)
on your calculator. Imagine an engineer solving this by hand for various parameters before calculators were invented. Then solve it on the nomogram here with a straightedge and compare your answers. When you’re finished, choose values of
\(r\)
,
\(l\)
and
\(s\)
and solve for
\(\alpha\)
. You’ll realize that a nomogram can solve even for implicit variables that cannot be isolated on one side of the equation!
How in the world was this nomogram designed? Somehow this layout of scales solves the equation for every combination of its values using just a straightedge. For the nine most common functional relationships, PyNomo generates vector-image nomograms in PDF form using simple but customizable scripts in which you provide the functions of the variables. Beyond this, experienced designers can use a tenth PyNomo option to draw nomograms with arbitrarily complicated layouts such as this one, and even linear and circular slide rules.
Designing nomograms is an enjoyable pursuit, much more so than in the past since PyNomo can provide the expert knowledge and also serve as the technical draftsman. And as described below, nomograms are very useful for a variety of applications even today.
Uses of Nomograms
¶
Nomograms have been used in an extensive array of applications. A sample includes
The original application by d’Ocagne, the automation of complicated “cut and fill” calculations for earth removal during the construction of the French national railway system. This was an important proof of concept, because the calculations are non-trivial and the results translated into significant savings of time, effort, and money.
The design of channels, pipes and weirs for regulating the flow of water.
The work of Lawrence Henderson, in which nomograms were used to correlate many different aspects of blood physiology. It was the first major use of nomograms in the United States and also the first medical nomograms anywhere. Nomograms continue to be used extensively in medical fields.
Ballistics calculations prior to fire control systems, where calculating time was critical.
Machine shop calculations, to convert blueprint dimensions and perform calculations based on material dimensions and - properties. These nomograms often included markings for standard dimensions and for available manufactured parts.
Statistics, for complicated calculations of properties of distributions and for operations research including the design of acceptance tests for quality control.
Operations Research, to obtain results in a variety of optimization problems.

data.title: What is a Lithium-ion capacitor?
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了JTEKT公司的锂离子电容器产品。

锂离子电容器结合了双电层电容器（EDLC）的正极和锂离子电池的负极，兼具较高能量密度和较长循环寿命（超10万次），同时比锂离子电池更安全。

与普通锂离子电容器相比，JTEKT的**Libuddy**产品大幅提升了功率密度和使用寿命，工作温度范围扩展至-40℃至85℃，循环寿命更达**100万次以上**，性能显著领先。

产品采用叠层结构，制造工艺与锂离子电池相似。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：锂离子电容器（Li-Ion Capacitors）的技术特性、应用场景与潜在问题

不同观点：
• **技术规格与使用注意事项**（rpaddock）：提供了真实数据表参数（标称电压4.0V、循环寿命>5万次、容量10F-1200F），强调焊接风险极高，且存在最低电压限制问题——低于该电压会缩短寿命，但目前缺乏量化数据。该技术由太阳诱电于2010年率先推出，但该公司已退出此市场。

• **安全顾虑**（SoftTalker）：大容量充电电容器具有危险性，与电池相比，电容器放电速率不受化学反应速度限制，因此放电更猛烈，隐含更高风险。

• **概念澄清**（supertroop）：提出电容器存储的是能量而非功率，指出标题或描述中"功率"与"能量"概念可能存在混用。

• **应用价值存疑**（mrDmrTmrJ）：以混合动力汽车轻量化为例，认为功率密度和循环寿命表现突出，但能量密度极低，实际应用场景有限。

• **信息不完整**（LorenPechtel）：指出讨论中完全未提及自放电率，这是评估电容器实用性的关键指标。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于该技术的实用价值——支持者看重其超长循环寿命和高功率密度，质疑者则认为低能量密度和缺失关键参数（如自放电率、最低电压限制的量化影响）使其实际应用受限。

48688081.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：锂离子电容器（Li-Ion Capacitors）的技术特性、应用场景与潜在问题

不同观点：
• **技术规格与使用注意事项**（rpaddock）：提供了真实数据表参数（标称电压4.0V、循环寿命>5万次、容量10F-1200F），强调焊接风险极高，且存在最低电压限制问题——低于该电压会缩短寿命，但目前缺乏量化数据。该技术由太阳诱电于2010年率先推出，但该公司已退出此市场。

• **安全顾虑**（SoftTalker）：大容量充电电容器具有危险性，与电池相比，电容器放电速率不受化学反应速度限制，因此放电更猛烈，隐含更高风险。

• **概念澄清**（supertroop）：提出电容器存储的是能量而非功率，指出标题或描述中"功率"与"能量"概念可能存在混用。

• **应用价值存疑**（mrDmrTmrJ）：以混合动力汽车轻量化为例，认为功率密度和循环寿命表现突出，但能量密度极低，实际应用场景有限。

• **信息不完整**（LorenPechtel）：指出讨论中完全未提及自放电率，这是评估电容器实用性的关键指标。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于该技术的实用价值——支持者看重其超长循环寿命和高功率密度，质疑者则认为低能量密度和缺失关键参数（如自放电率、最低电压限制的量化影响）使其实际应用受限。

主要讨论点：美国政府限制最新AI模型访问权限（仅批准机构可用，个人用户被排除），引发对创新、地缘竞争和权力滥用的广泛讨论。

不同观点：

• **反对政府管控（自由派/创新优先）**：认为此举缺乏透明的政策框架，政府将成为创新瓶颈，可能"钦定赢家输家"，且无任何公开的行政令或立法依据。

• **看空美国AI主导地位**：认为此举正在加速开源模型和中国模型的崛起。类比PostgreSQL vs Oracle——OpenAI/Anthropic向高端企业市场收缩，最终将失去技术优势和市场份额。

• **担忧腐败与权力滥用**：当前白宫的行事风格使"凭关系审批"成为可能，政治因素可能左右哪些公司获得访问权限。

• **个人用户被边缘化**：普通订阅用户已无法获得前沿模型，部分人表示将转向开源或中国模型（DeepSeek、GLM等），实际体验差异并不值得维持订阅。

• **地缘政治联动视角**：将此与关税、欧洲云主权觉醒、美元武器化等并列，认为美国正在重复中国打压本国科技业（阿里、滴滴、腾讯等）的模式，只是换了方向。

• **安全威胁论（少数支持管控）**：认为此举可能源于内部评估发现模型已可辅助生化武器开发，管控有其现实依据。

补充讨论：欧盟被认为是最大的潜在受害方——若既受中美双重管控又缺乏自主模型，五年内可能在AI上全面落伍。

3. GEMM从基础分块到SOTA优化（TMA流水线、Warp特化、2-CTA集群）
4. FlashAttention 4完整实现（双MMA、在线softmax、因果掩码、GQA）

本书强调"先懂硬件，再建内核"的系统性学习路径。

48643459.article_content:
Modern GPU Programming For MLSys
Contents
Modern GPU Programming For MLSys
#
Machine learning systems sit at the heart of modern AI workloads. In these systems, performance
often comes down to the quality of a small number of GPU kernels. Attention kernels, LLM prefill
and decode kernels, low-precision block-scaled GEMMs, fused MoE layers, and other large fused
kernels all directly shape end-to-end speed in both training and serving.
To make these kernels fast, however, we need more than a list of optimization tricks. Modern GPUs
are no longer simple variations of the same old design. Recent architectures introduce richer
memory spaces, new access patterns, and increasingly specialized execution units. To program them
well, we need both a clear mental model of the hardware and a practical understanding of how
high-performance kernels are built. This book is about developing both.
The book follows a simple progression: first understand the GPU hardware, then learn the
programming model we will use, and finally build state-of-the-art kernels step by step. Our main
target is the Blackwell generation, and our main running examples are fast matrix multiplication
(GEMM) and FlashAttention. Along the way, we will also study the core ingredients behind GPU
optimization: data layout, asynchronous data movement, and asynchronous coordination.
The material grows out of the
Machine Learning Systems
course series
at Carnegie Mellon University. To make the ideas easier to study and easier to run, this book uses
the
TIRx
Python DSL to build real GPU kernel examples step by step. TIRx stays close to the
hardware, which lets us reason about low-level control while still learning through runnable code.
How This Book Is Organized
#
Part I, Understanding the GPU.
This part introduces the overall organization of the GPU,
general recipes for writing fast kernels, and key concepts such as data layout, asynchronous
memory operations, and coordination. It builds the hardware intuition that the rest of the book
relies on.
Part II, TIRx Overview.
This part introduces the key elements of TIRx, which serve as the
foundation for the code examples throughout the book.
Part III, GEMM: Tiled to SOTA.
A complete guide to optimizing a tiled GEMM, built up through
TMA pipelining, persistent scheduling, warp specialization, and 2-CTA clusters.
Part IV, Flash Attention 4.
A complete attention kernel built from the Part III techniques:
two MMAs with softmax between them, online-softmax rescaling, causal masking, and GQA.
Reference.
TIRx language reference and compiler internals.

data.title: The "Bizarre Headgear" exhibit at the Sam Noble museum
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 萨姆·诺贝尔博物馆举办了一个名为"奇异头饰：角龙类与非凡头骨的演化"的临时特展。展览以角龙类恐龙为核心，展出了从早期小型种（如鹦鹉嘴龙、辽角龙、原角龙）到大型晚期种（如犹他角龙、戟龙、牛角龙）的头骨、骨架及复原雕塑，涵盖许多鲜为公众熟知的物种。展览同时陈列了大量哺乳动物、鲸类、长鼻目等非恐龙动物头骨（逾65件），通过对比展示"奇异头饰"在动物界的广泛演化。展品密度极高，据作者统计共有5具恐龙骨架和16件其他恐龙头骨，配以Shane Foulkes的雕塑和Andrey Atuchin的绘画，说明牌设计精良。参观者和古生物学家均对展览内容之丰富印象深刻。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一张恐龙头部造型图片的各种联想与反应

不同观点：
• **科幻联想**（keeda）：看到图片后联想到"铁血战士"（Predator）与恐龙对战的电影场景，认为这会是个酷炫的创意。
• **科学准确性质疑**（xvedejas）：提出恐龙复原图是否应加入羽毛的问题，认为学界正朝着有羽毛的恐龙形象发展，但也承认具体细节可能证据不足，难以精确还原。
• **文字误读**（giarc）：将标题"headgear"误读为牙科器械，并认为以此为主题的展览同样会很有趣。
• **双关笑话**（destinator）："a head of its time"（同时暗含"ahead of its time"即"超前于时代"），以冷笑话收尾。

补充讨论：评论整体较轻松幽默，并无实质争议。xvedejas关于羽毛的提问是唯一涉及科学内容的讨论点，但未有人跟进回应，属于未展开的话题。

incredible
May 15, 2026
An imposing view of a juvenile

.
As threatened
, I was in Oklahoma at the tail end of last week and over the weekend, mostly to give talks. My Friday evening public lecture was on horned dinosaurs, and it was tied in with the launch of a temporary exhibit called “Bizarre Headgear: Ceratopsians and the Evolution of Extraordinary Skulls”. I’ll cover the talks in another post; this one is about that exhibit.
From the museum’s central atrium, there are a couple of passages into the special exhibition gallery that houses “Bizarre Headgear”. My preferred way in is the second doorway, farther from the front of the museum, which puts you face-to-face with pterosaurs and hell pigs. This sets up the basic division of the room: mostly Mesozoic and mostly dinos to the left, mostly Cenozoic and mostly mammals to the right (with a few exceptions, like the
Synthetoceras
visible on the back wall).
From there, turn left and you’ll see horned dinosaurs and many other interesting critters. A
lot
of them.
Turn right and you’ll see a lot more non-dinosaurs, mostly extinct and extant mammals with a smattering of non-mammals.
I was there to yap about horned dinos, and the exhibit does not slack in this department, starting with this charming side-by-side skeletal reconstruction and lift restoration of
Psittacosaurus
. The sculpture is by Shane Foulkes, and it looks like a real animal.

Liaoceratops
,

,

, and
Protoceratops
. These are little
Aquilops
-alikes from Asia. Back in 2014, Farke et al. got this topology:

I’d never seen so many of these adorable little weirdos in one place. Heck, I’d never even seen casts of
Liaoceratops
and
Auroraceratops
in person. So it was nice to get acquainted with the aunts and cousins of
Aquilops
.
The ceratopsian show continues with a pair of
Protoceratops
skeletons, followed by skulls of
Zuniceratops
,
Diabloceratops
,
Kosmoceratops
, and a cool
Utahceratops
with some soft tissue reconstructed. There’s also a mounted skeleton of
Torosaurus
, and the juvenile
Utahceratops
shown at the top of the post. This diversity of critters from across the ceratopsian tree was clutch when I helped lead a student tour on Monday. And it was nice to see a lot of animals that weren’t described when I was growing up, and that the average museum-goer might be less familiar with —
Diabloceratops
instead of
Centrosaurus
or
Styracosaurus
,
Kosmoceratops
and
Utahceratops
in place of
Triceratops
and
Chasmosaurus
.
The exhibit has a lot more than just skulls and skeletons. There are loads of sculptures, both life-sized fleshed-out heads and miniatures showing the whole animal, like this
Pachyrhinosaurus
. And lots of wall art. I believe all of the sculptures are by Shane Foulkes (and apologies if I missed anyone else). Most of the paintings are by Andrey Atuchin, but there is at least one Mark Hallett piece in the exhibit:
Synthetoceras
being menaced by an amphicyonid ‘bear-dog’.
The mostly-mammals, mostly-extant side of the exhibit is equally impressive. I’m including fewer photos from that side, because this is already a long post, but I counted at least 65 skulls of non-dinosaurs, including 3 proboscideans and 5 cetaceans. Invertebrates even get a look in, with some of the more baroquely-horned beetles. I nipped into the exhibit while it was still being set up to get some photos for my talk, like this awesome array of African bovids. All of these non-ceratopsians are there to put the evolution of bizarre headgear in dinosaurs into context, and to show that dinos were not incomprehensible monsters, but animals whose anatomy and ecology we can understand, or at least make pretty good inferences about. The signage is uniformly excellent — discreet, informative, and attractively laid out, with a consistent arrangement and color palette.
As long as we’re keeping score, I counted 5 mounted dinosaur skeletons, and 16 other dinosaur skulls. This exhibit is
stacked
. Every single person I talked to about it, including other paleontologists, staff, security guards, and museum visitors, volunteered something along the lines of “Holy cow, that is a lot of amazing stuff.” The sheer density and diversity of material on display has a qualitative impact, which gave me the feeling of walking through a cabinet of curiositie

data.title: LaTeX.wasm: LaTeX Engines in Browsers
data.author: theanonymousone
data.article_summary:
**LaTeX.wasm** 是一个将 LaTeX 排版引擎（PdfTeX 和 XeTeX）编译为 WebAssembly、使其能在浏览器中运行的开源项目。

主要特点：
- 输出结果与 TexLive/MikTeX 完全一致
- 运行速度仅比原生二进制慢约 2 倍
- 支持通过 `<script>` 标签直接引入使用
- 支持所见即所得（WYSIWYG）编辑

使用流程简单：引入 JS 文件 → 初始化引擎 → 上传 .tex 文件 → 调用 `compileLaTeX()` 获取 PDF 二进制结果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在浏览器中运行 LaTeX 引擎（SwiftLaTeX）的可行性与实际体验

不同观点：
• **看好潜力**（jerf）：认为 WASM 成熟后有望用于改进浏览器排版，LaTeX 可能在此领域占据一席之地，但长期能否守住优势存疑。

• **技术已有先例**（dunham）：指出 web2js 项目早已将 TeX Pascal 代码编译为 WASM（压缩后约 88KB），并能在浏览器渲染 DVI 输出，SwiftLaTeX 并非首创。

• **实际使用有问题**（stschaef、williamstein）：用户直接遭遇错误（找不到格式文件），WYSIWYG 编辑器页面长期显示"正在修复"，疑因文档损坏风险被下线。

• **期待离线与生态完善**（andai、joshjob42）：希望发行版更精简开箱即用，同时期待 LuaLaTeX 支持及完整 LaTeX 生态在线/桌面端普及。

• **质疑 WASM 价值**（casey2）：项目仍需安装且不跨平台，与 WASM "一次编译到处运行"的初衷相悖，讽刺意味明显。

• **技术困惑**（christoff12）：不理解为何 BibTeX 需要编译三次才能得到正确引用，认为设计存在疑问。

补充讨论：hulitu 嘲讽浏览器打印能力退化十年，认为用浏览器输出排版精美的 PDF 本身就是悖论；psc007 则简单追问为何没有 npm 包，反映出开发者对工具链集成的基本诉求。

48650550.article_content:
Fork me on GitHub
LaTeX.wasm: LaTeX Engines in Browsers
100% Browser
PdfTeX and XeTeX written in 100% WebAssembly and run in browsers.
Compatibility
Produce exact same output you would get from TexLive or MikTeX.
Library Support
Simply include a script tag and use PdfTeX or XeTeX in your own webpage.
WYSIWYG
Support WYSIWYG editing on LaTeX documents using XeTeX engine.
Speed
Run merely 2X slower than native binaries.
Open Source
Completely Open Source. You can find the code on
GitHub
.
Select a demo:
PdfTeX basic demo (IEEEConf)
XeTeX basic demo (acmart)
XeTeX Chinese/Japanese demo
XeTeX TrueType demo
XeTeX Tikz demo
XeTeX Beamer demo
PdfTeX Beamer demo
PdfTeX UTF8 demo
PdfTeX Tikz demo
PdfTeX CV demo
It may take a few minutes to download template files for the first time. Please be patient
Installation
Step 1: Download latest release from
Github
. Extract the files and put them into
your webpage directory.
Step 2: Include the src tag in your page.
<script src="PdfTeXEngine.js"></script>
Step 3: Initial the engine.
const engine = new LaTeXEngine();
await engine.loadEngine();
Step 4: Load the tex files/pictures/fonts to engines.
const engine = new LaTeXEngine();
engine.writeMemFSFile("main.tex", "\documentclass{...");
Step 5: Set the main file and fire the compilation.
engine.setEngineMainFile("main.tex");
let r = await engine.compileLaTeX(); // r contains PDF binray and compilation log.
APIs
async loadEngine(): Promise<void&gt.
Load the webassembly engine.
isReady(): boolean.
Check whether the engine is ready to compile documents.
writeMemFSFile(filename: string, srccode: string | Uint8Array).
Upload source codes / assets to the engine.
makeMemFSFolder(folder: string).
Create a directory.
setEngineMainFile(filename: string).
Tell the engine which latex file is the entry file.
compileLaTeX():Promise<CompileResult>.
Start compiling LaTeX documents and return CompileResult.
flushCache().
Purge all the files uploaded.
closeWorker().
Shutdown the engine.

data.title: Medical students are using popular research tool to pump out misleading studies
data.author: rndsignals
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：医学生被要求发表研究论文的制度问题，以及由此引发的学术质量下滑和激励机制扭曲。

不同观点：
• **制度根源论**（jmyeet、bagelbob432）：Step 1 改为通过/不通过后，研究成果成为住院医匹配的关键差异化指标，导致医学生大量堆砌低质量论文。这是系统性激励扭曲的直接后果。

• **医学生不该搞科研**（currymj、fn-mote）：医学教育和科研训练是两套体系，MD-PhD 项目的存在本身就说明两者不可兼得。住院医录取把同行评审当求职筛选工具，是对科研体系的滥用。

• **改革方向：重奖复现、轻奖发表**（whizzter、spchampion2）：学术激励应转向审查和复现论文，而非发表数量；Medicare 培训经费不应用于资助研究，研究资金应来自专门渠道。

• **科学公信力危机**（zemvpferreira、googaar）：Goodhart 定律早已预示今日困境——指标一旦成为目标即失效。学界自以为超脱于激励扭曲之上，是一种傲慢。

• **标准底线问题**（BrtByte、harvey9）：对有多年大学教育背景的医学生而言，研究设计如此粗劣令人震惊，至少应公开查询方式和分析偏差。

补充讨论：abeppu 指出一个方法论悖论——用一篇极端劣质论文来证明"研究质量整体下滑"，本身就是一种挑选性证据。bigmattystyles 则从患者视角补充：LLM 提供的虚假医疗希望与低质研究的危害性质相近，都在制造不可靠的信息幻觉。

data.title: Data centers trigger voter backlash
data.author: randycupertino
data.article_summary:
美国数据中心项目正引发选民强烈反弹，并开始影响选举结果。

在犹他州，共和党参议院主席J. Stuart Adams因支持"Stratos"大型数据中心项目而在初选中落败。该项目拟建于大盐湖附近，规模庞大，需耗电高达9吉瓦（超过犹他州目前全州用电量），引发当地居民强烈反对。多名支持该项目的县级官员也在初选中相继落败。

政治学者Cassino指出，疫情后能源价格已成为选民最关注的民生议题，而"AI数据中心拉高你的电费"这一说法极具煽动性。民调显示，57%的美国人反对在自己社区建设数据中心，约七成人反对在当地兴建。

数据中心曾被视为带来就业和税收的经济利好，如今却因耗水、耗电、占地及政府补贴等问题成为政治负担，且反对声音已超越党派界限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据中心建设引发的社区反对浪潮——其背后的真实驱动力是什么？

不同观点：

• **反对情绪源于信息操控与非理性**（miiiiiike、madrox、socalgal2）：反对者被社交媒体恐慌内容煽动，忽视实际数据。有人怀疑是中俄的信息战或网红为流量制造对立。数据中心对比高尔夫球场在用地、用水上根本不值一提。

• **民主程序遭到破坏是核心问题**（thewillowcat、cosmic_cheese）：政客在签署NDA保密协议后强推项目，绕过公众知情权。问题不在于数据中心本身，而在于决策过程不透明、不民主。

• **就业与经济才是民众真正关心的**（yardie）：AI公司高管承认技术会造成大规模失业，却拒绝回答数据中心能带来多少本地就业。Jensen Huang是少数例外，其余人回避了这一核心问题。

• **愤怒的根源是贫富不均，而非技术本身**（munificent）：若AI由成千上万小企业运营，反弹不会如此激烈。真正激怒民众的是极少数亿万富翁攫取巨额利益，这与Luigi Mangione案的社会情绪同根同源。

• **建设需求本身存在泡沫**（e40）：大量数据中心基于AI需求的过度乐观预测，可能永远不会建成或无法盈利，本质上是新一轮淘金热。

• **反对一切建设是民主的结构性缺陷**（arjie、teravor）：无论住房、风电、铁路还是数据中心，选民总会反对。民主在信息战时代愈发脆弱，难以做出需要长远判断的决策。

补充讨论：地缘政治压力（中国AI竞争）与本地民意之间形成张力，部分人认为即便数据中心有缺点，输掉AI竞赛的代价更大。

A wave of voter anger over massive data center projects is beginning to reshape U.S. politics, with local officials and senior lawmakers losing elections after backing controversial developments tied to the artificial intelligence boom.
In Utah on Wednesday, State Senate President J. Stuart Adams—one of the most powerful Republicans in the state—lost his primary election after supporting a major data center development near the Great Salt Lake, in one of the clearest signs yet of the growing political risks tied to the industry.
At the local level, the fallout was just as direct. “Do I think that the data center vote cost me the election? Yes I do,” former Box Elder County Commissioner Lee Perry said after conceding his primary race, after voting to advance the same project.
Read More
on
News
The defeats of Adams and multiple county officials tied to the proposal suggest that opposition to data centers is no longer confined to planning disputes—but is emerging as a voting issue capable of reshaping elections.
...
Utah's Stratos Project Controversy Explained
The controversy in Utah centered on a sprawling proposed data center campus, known as the Stratos project, planned near the Great Salt Lake.
Described as one of the largest data centers in the world, and backed by
Shark Tank
investor Kevin O’Leary, the Stratos development would have spanned tens of thousands of acres in Box Elder County’s Hansel Valley. The project would ultimately require up to 9 gigawatts of power—more electricity than the entire state of Utah currently uses, according to
The Guardian
, although O'Leary later told NBC News he would be willing to shrink the project.
Adams became a focal point for opposition after backing the development in his role leading a state authority that approved early plans for the site, drawing criticism from residents who said officials ignored local concerns.
Those concerns translated into political consequences. Adams, who had previously won reelection comfortably, was defeated by a challenger who ran in part on opposing the project. At the county level, commissioners who voted to advance the project also lost their primaries.
Energy Prices Are the Current Face of Affordability
Dan Cassino, a professor of government and politics at Fairleigh Dickinson University and executive director of the FDU Poll, said data centers have already become a major issue in primary elections as affordability has become central to U.S. politics and energy prices have become “the current face of affordability.”
“Since the pandemic, affordability has become a key issue in U.S. politics, and energy prices are the current face of affordability,” Cassino told
Newsweek
. “In our polling, voters support anything to bring down their energy bills, but banning data centers is pretty much the most popular option.”
Cassino said data centers are not the only reason energy prices have risen, describing them as “only a small part of it.” But he said the argument that “’AI data centers are eating your electricity’” gives candidates a “simple and compelling story,” especially when voters are already skeptical of AI.
He said the politics of the issue do not fall neatly along partisan lines. Democrats who have traditionally emphasized balancing economic development with environmental concerns are facing pressure from the party’s left flank, while Republicans who have long argued that reducing regulation helps growth are now facing voters who believe new development could affect them personally through higher energy prices.
“None of this would matter if voters liked what they were getting from the data centers, but they don't see the benefit. ‘You'll pay higher energy prices, but either you'll lose your job or your 401k will collapse’ isn't a deal most voters are eager to take,” Cassino added.
Data Center Concerns Become Political Issue
Data centers—once promoted by politicians as economic wins—are becoming a political liability for elected officials across the country, cutting across party lines and shaping election outcomes in ways few expected just a year ago.
A Reuters/Ipsos survey in June found that 57 percent of Americans would oppose a data center being built in their community, with just 14 percent comfortable living near one. Meanwhile, a Gallup survey conducted earlier this year found that around seven in ten Americans oppose the construction of local data centers, highlighting a growing gap between national demand for AI infrastructure and local acceptance.
The projects promise jobs and tax revenue. But they also bring concerns about water use, electricity demand, land use and taxpayer subsidies—issues that are now driving organized opposition and, increasingly, votes.

data.title: You can't unit test for taste
data.author: kalli
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了作者为跑步应用"In the Long Run"构建兴趣点（POI）数据管道的过程。

应用让用户通过累计Strava跑步里程，在世界著名路线上虚拟前行，并在交互地图上显示进度。为丰富地图内容，作者需要大规模的兴趣点数据源。

**技术方案：**
- 数据源：GeoNames（知名开源地理数据库，含Creative Commons许可）
- 技术栈：Python + Apache Parquet + DuckDB
- AI辅助：与Claude协作设计管道架构和逐步实现

**数据处理流程：**
1. 下载GeoNames原始数据，过滤掉行政区划，保留公园、历史遗址、城堡、山峰等有意义的类别
2. 通过人口和海拔阈值进一步筛选
3. 利用Wikipedia链接（隐藏在alternateNames数据集中）作为知名度信号
4. 从1300万条原始记录筛减至约72.5万条候选POI

**关键经验：**
- AI最终只是辅助角色，而非核心功能
- 分阶段构建规范/计划，每个里程碑开新会话，避免大上下文降低质量
- 项目中适量引入新工具（Parquet、DuckDB）是最佳学习方式

文章截至此处仍在继续介绍第二步处理流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI辅助开发中"品味"（taste）能否被量化、外化并传递给AI，以及人类判断力的不可替代性。

不同观点：

• **品味无法完全外化**（trjordan、brap、TimXare）：人类知识和审美无法完整写下来，即使写成规则，AI也只会机械遵守而无法泛化。"品味"就是你忘记写或根本写不出来的那部分规格。

• **品味可以被部分工具化**（cadamsdotcom、fotoblur）：可以将"好设计"的标准编写成脚本（如品牌色彩检查、pre-commit钩子），让AI在提交前获得自动反馈，从而间接约束其行为。

• **品味可以从大量数据中涌现**（timroman、jt2190）：单个spec无法体现品味，但积累100个项目spec后AI能逐渐习得；LLM或许能追踪人类会遗漏的大量细节，帮助量化品味。

• **AI缺乏用户体验判断力**（ChrisMarshallNY）：AI无法像开发者那样持续测试、感知细微摩擦点，"vibe-coded"的应用难以真正可靠。

• **单元测试本身也无法覆盖所有逻辑**（layer8、pjmlp）：这一局限并非AI独有，单元测试本身就无法枚举所有输入状态，TDD也非万能。

补充讨论：zamalek用"Reckless Ben案"做了一个有趣的类比——AI给出了法律上"极度聪明但几乎没有律师会建议提交"的论点，印证了AI在判断"适度性"和社会情境方面的短板，与品味问题高度相关。

I’m building
In the Long Run
where runners do
virtual
runs on famous routes around the world. The app tallies up your Strava mileage and plots your total distance as progress against country- or continent-spanning routes. The intention is to provide long-term inspiration and motivation; life is a marathon, not a sprint. You can have a bad month or season but still make progress on your virtual traversal of the world.
The app shows your progress on interactive maps, which lets users do some exploring of their own. But I had long wanted to enrich the maps with interesting sights or historical sites. For routes I was familiar with I could build such lists myself but that doesn’t scale to routes spanning countries I am not familiar with. So I set out to find a data source for points of interest that I could build a pipeline off. Along the way I wrestled with taste and biases, and fought a hallucinating llm. I initially thought AI would be the feature, but it ended up merely in a supporting role alongside other signals and data processing mainstays.
Dataset and toolset
#
GeoNames
was an obvious starting point, an extensive data source with locations, categories and links. The full data set can be downloaded and has a Creative Commons licence. So with my friend Claude I set about building a pipeline to go from the raw dumps to serving relevant points of interest to users of
In the Long Run
.
We used Python as the programming language (had good library support for the tasks at hand), stored processed data locally as Apache Parquet files and used DuckDB as the query layer.
1
This was my first time using both Parquet and DuckDB but the ergonomics of both felt good and Claude introduced me to their features step by step (and most of the DuckDB work was SQL that I am very familiar with). In general I find adding one or two new tools or technologies to a project is the best way to learn. If the entire stack is new to you the learning curve will be too steep and it might put you off the project entirely. AI coding agents change this calculus somewhat, but even then I find having a handle on
most
of the technologies being used lets me steer the agent better and make informed decisions instead of blindly following its lead.
Point of interest feature screenshot for a runner on Route 66 near Springfield, Illinois.
I built a project plan with Claude before starting the implementation, outlining the different steps of the pipeline and feature work. As we went along we then built a spec/plan for each step that we could iterate on as we learned more from earlier work. This also meant I could start new agent sessions for each milestone. Condensing results from the previous milestones into short context and instructions for the next step gets you faster and better responses (I find big contexts quickly degrade the quality of agent work).
Notability and notable biases
#
To begin with we downloaded and unzipped all the
required files from Geonames
and set up gitignores for the data files as most are too large to be version controlled.
The first step of processing was joining the downloaded files on the relevant columns and filtering out rows that were not useful for our purposes. For instance we excluded administrative divisions: countries, states, regions etc. We also selected specific feature codes that we thought would be most interesting: parks, historic sites, castles, monuments, mountains, etc.
2
Finally we added a population filter on populated places and an elevation filter on mountains. I’m sure this led to some false negatives, but we wanted a rough first draft.
Somewhat unintuitively the
alternateNames.txt
Geonames dataset includes Wikipedia links (where
isolanguage=link
and
alternate_name like %en.wikipedia.org%
, this usecase feels bolted on to their schema after the fact but it is very helpful data to have). We used this as a notoriety/relevance signal, and it also provided texts that we could build blurbs from as Wikipedia summaries also have a Creative Commons licence.
We built a basic sanity check for this pipeline step that helped us verify we weren’t skipping notable landmarks, this let us tweak some of the filtering. For instance, the first draft pulled in the Australian rural locality
Stonehenge
but not the prehistoric megalithic structure (its more famous namesake). When working in English you also want to make sure you pull in the relevant alternate names / languages and use the relevant Wikipedia URL as a cross reference (GeoNames stores the canonical name in the local language).
The final result of this step was a parquet file with around 725 thousand rows for points of interest globally. A significant reduction from the 13 million in the full original set we started out with.
Populated places are the bulk of the Geonames dataset. But we don't want the points of interest to just show every town, village and hamlet on the way.

data.title: Show HN: I made Google Trends for Hacker News by indexing 18 years of comments
data.author: ytkimirti
data.article_summary:
**Hacker Trends** 是一个可视化工具，追踪18年来（45M条帖子和评论）任意话题、工具或人物在 Hacker News 上的讨论热度变化。

核心功能：
- 输入关键词生成时间趋势折线图，支持多词叠加对比
- 点击或拖拽时间轴可筛选特定时间段
- 图表下方展示对应的原始帖子和评论，可按热度、讨论量、时间排序
- 后端基于 Upstash Redis Search 构建

内置了大量经典对比案例，如 OpenAI vs Anthropic、Docker vs Kubernetes、Vim vs VSCode、ChatGPT vs DeepSeek 等，直观呈现技术圈的"朝代更迭"规律。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HN Trends——一个可视化Hacker News历史评论关键词趋势的工具

不同观点：

• **功能认可与定位澄清**：多数人认为项目创意有趣、执行良好（dom96、joshmaker、linmer），但Aachen指出它与Google Trends本质不同——搜索量反映用户意图，而文本频率反映"值得书写的话题"，二者不可混用。

• **技术稳定性问题**：simonpure和kaelyx反映上线初期出现504/502错误（Vercel超时、Upstash数据库限流），说明项目承受了较大流量压力。

• **数据呈现的局限性**：arjie和joshmaker都提出需要**相对化/归一化**选项——绝对数量会被站点整体增长掩盖，应支持"占比"视图而非仅显示原始计数。

• **功能改进建议**：
  - linmer：点击图表跳转到对应日期的HN页面
  - kpw94：加入正负情感分析，区分"好评提及"与"差评提及"
  - sinuhe69：用AI将同义词归类，如"autopilot"应涵盖"self driving"、"FSD"等
  - bluecoconut：缩略图与完整图的颜色分配不一致，影响理解

• **已知Bug**：gslepak发现对比图表在2018-10后数据截断；paravz发现"Prometheus"词条混入了错误的同名词条（去除CO2项目）。

补充讨论：zX41ZdbW提供了公开的ClickHouse HN数据库接口，可用于构建类似服务；smalltorch介绍了功能相似的自建HN克隆项目Torum。

核心功能：

内置了大量经典对比案例，如 OpenAI vs Anthropic、Docker vs Kubernetes、Vim vs VSCode、ChatGPT vs DeepSeek 等，直观呈现技术圈的"朝代更迭"规律。

data.title: A little bird told her: scientist wins $100k prize for decoding birdsong
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary:
加州大学伯克利分校科学家朱莉·埃利（Julie Elie）因破译斑胸草雀的鸣声语言，荣获2026年度10万美元Coller-Dolittle跨物种交流奖。

她历经十余年研究，识别出斑胸草雀的11种核心叫声及其含义，发现这些鸟类能通过叫声表达身份和行为，并借助个体"签名"相互辨认。更关键的是，鸟儿犯错时往往混淆意义相似的叫声，而非音调相似的叫声，表明它们能理解叫声的含义。

该奖项由Jeremy Coller基金会与特拉维夫大学于2024年联合设立，并设有1000万美元大奖，目标是实现人与动物的双向交流。随着AI技术的快速发展，奖项创始人Coller乐观预计2030年前将实现这一突破。

A little bird told her: scientist wins $100,000 prize for decoding birdsong
Julie Elie worked out how zebra finches announce who they are, what they are doing and use individual signatures
Ian Sample
Science editor

First published on Fri 26 Jun 2026 02.51 EDT
Share
Prefer the Guardian on Google
A scientist who decoded the vocalisations that a bird uses to communicate has won a $100,000 prize for making progress towards a world in which humans can talk to the animals – without being met with a blank response.
Dr Julie Elie at the University of California, Berkeley, was awarded the 2026 Coller-Dolittle prize for two-way interspecies communication after working out the 11 core calls in the zebra finch vocabulary and their meanings.
Her work revealed how the birds announce who they are and what they are doing, and recognise one another regardless of what they are saying by using individual signatures. She also found that at times, the birds confused calls with similar meanings more than those that sounded the same.
“I’m really super-honoured,” Elie said on winning the prize, adding that she hoped the work was a step forwards in the “great endeavour” to communicate with animals. Prof Yossi Yovel, a zoologist at Tel Aviv University and chair of the panel of judges, said the work marked “a key moment in the field”.
The prize was launched in 2024 by the Jeremy Coller Foundation, which promotes awareness of animal welfare and animal sentience, in partnership with Tel Aviv University. Beyond the annual prizes for progress, the foundation has established a $10m grand prize for cracking the problem of two-way human-animal communication.
Masturbation among birds is ‘natural’ and should not be punished, say experts
Read more
Elie decided to study zebra finches because they are so vocal – meaning they produce plenty of data. “The question I asked myself when hearing these chatty songbirds was what are they saying?” she said.
For more than a decade, Elie observed and recorded the sounds the birds made and classified the calls according to the situation and the bird that made them. She then used machine learning to analyse what and how information was encoded in the calls. Finally, she ran tests that showed the birds agreed with her classification.
In one test, zebra finches were played various calls from their repertoire when they tapped a button. Some calls were followed by a reward of some seeds. As the test went on, the birds learned to tap the button to skip unrewarding calls. It’s similar to scrolling videos on social media, Elie said, moving on when the start of the video looks dull.
The birds occasionally made mistakes, but when that happened, they often confused calls that had the same meaning rather than the same sound. “Their responses indicated they have a mental imagery of the meaning of their vocalisations,” Elie said. “In other words, that they understand the meaning of their call types.”
Prof Jonathan Birch, a philosopher at the London School of Economics, who was on the judging panel, said Elie had done “absolutely phenomenal work” for more than 15 years, “not just building up a dictionary of the 11 ‘core words’ of the zebra finch’s vocabulary, but also asking the finches themselves, through ingenious experimental techniques, whether she’s got the meanings right. It’s a stunning example of how to move rigorously from recording thousands of calls to understanding their meanings.”
Other scientists shortlisted for the prize included a French team that showed how African striped mice reveal their identity through ultrasonic squeaks; a Swiss-US team that found bonobos combine their calls into sequences that resemble human sentences; and another French team that worked with researchers in Côte d’Ivoire to understand chimpanzee hoos and yelps.

A French team that worked with researchers in Côte d’Ivoire was shortlisted for understanding the hoos and yelps of chimpanzees.
Photograph: Danita Delimont/Alamy
Advances in artificial intelligence are transforming hopes that humans could one day communicate with animals in a coherent and meaningful way. Armed with machine learning algorithms, researchers are deciphering how animal calls convey meaning. But there is a long way to go to reach back and forth communication, Yovel said.

data.title: Hey Nico, you didn't vibe code your data room but stole it from Papermark
data.author: mmunj
data.article_summary:
**主要内容：**

开源项目 Papermark 的创始人 Marc Seitz 公开指控 YC 创业公司创始人 Nico 抄袭其开源及企业授权代码，用于构建自家的"数据室"（data room）产品，而非如宣称的那样通过 AI 辅助编程（vibe coding）自主开发。Marc 要求对方立即下架侵权产品，并点名 YC 掌门人 Garry Tan，认为此事不仅构成版权和许可证侵权，更是欺诈行为，有损 YC 社区声誉。该推文获得近 39 万次浏览，引发大量讨论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YC旗下初创公司Dataroom被指控抄袭开源项目Papermark（AGPL协议）的代码和设计，创始人Nico Laqua否认直接复制代码，引发社区广泛争议。

不同观点：
• **创始人辩护立场**：Nico声称未手动复制任何代码，产品从零开发，只是参考了同类软件的设计，否认侵权指控。

• **批评方立场**：截图显示页面布局、文案几乎一字不差，指出"让AI克隆他人项目"本质上仍是复制，区别只是谁按的键盘。Papermark已发出停止侵权函，要求下架产品。

• **AI代劳免责论的质疑**：多人指出，用LLM生成"1:1复刻"同样构成侵权，"我们自己没复制，是AI复制的"这一辩护站不住脚，甚至可能成为新型侵权案例的测试场。

• **技术层面存疑**：有人（bushido）提出两款产品的设计高度相似可能是因为都使用了ShadCN通用UI组件库，并非直接抄袭，强调相似性证据尚不充分。

• **AGPL许可证问题**：即便是AI生成，若实际复现了AGPL代码，则衍生产品必须同样开源。违反AGPL是明确的法律问题，而非仅道德问题。

• **YC生态信任危机**：有声音认为此事折射出YC近年吸引的创始人质量下滑，若对明显侵权行为不表态，将损害整个YC社区声誉。

补充讨论：此事引申出一个更广泛的问题——AI时代是否为代码抄袭提供了新的"洗白"通道？若恶意行为者用他人私有代码训练模型再输出，现有法律能否有效追责，尚无定论。

data.title: LastPass notifies users of yet another data breach
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary: LastPass再次通知用户发生数据泄露，此次事件源于其合作伙伴、市场调研公司Klue遭黑客入侵。泄露信息包括客户姓名、电话、电子邮件、地址及销售支持数据，但密码保险库未受影响。LastPass已撤销员工对Klue的访问权限、轮换API令牌并报警调查。公司提醒用户警惕钓鱼攻击和社会工程攻击，并公布了相关攻击者IP地址和邮件域名。这是LastPass继2015年和2022年之后再次发生安全事件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LastPass客户数据因第三方CRM服务商Klue遭黑客攻击而泄露，引发对LastPass可信度及密码管理器选择的讨论。

不同观点：

• **此次泄露性质不严重**：paranoidrobot、insanitybit等人指出，泄露的只是CRM联系信息（姓名、邮箱、电话），并非密码库数据，且将客户数据交给销售CRM工具是行业普遍做法，不应过度解读。

• **LastPass已失去信任**：jagged-chisel、john_strinlai等人认为，LastPass多次出现安全事故（尤其是2022年密码库泄露），任何在那之后仍选用LastPass的公司都难以获得同情；woadwarrior01用"First0wned"讽刺其屡次被入侵。

• **质疑数据共享必要性**：bradley13和felooboolooomba质问LastPass为何将客户数据交给Klue，认为至少应做匿名化处理。

• **推荐本地/离线密码管理器**：vrighter、username135、bradley13等强烈推荐KeePass系离线工具，认为在线密码管理器本身就是风险；MetroWind直言无法理解为何要把密码存在别人的服务器上。

• **推荐其他在线替代品**：giancarlostoro推荐Bitwarden，hbn推荐Enpass（数据存于用户自己的云存储，无集中数据库），fusslo则采用"忘记密码+临时重置"策略规避风险。

补充讨论：此次攻击实为供应链事件，除LastPass外，Gong、HackerOne、Snyk等多家知名公司也受波及；争议焦点在于——这究竟是LastPass自身问题，还是整个行业使用第三方销售工具的普遍风险？

As a result, LastPass is recommending that customers “remain vigilant of potential phishing attacks or social engineering attempts” leveraging the compromised information. • **此次泄露性质不严重**：paranoidrobot、insanitybit等人指出，泄露的只是CRM联系信息（姓名、邮箱、电话），并非密码库数据，且将客户数据交给销售CRM工具是行业普遍做法，不应过度解读。

• **LastPass已失去信任**：jagged-chisel、john_strinlai等人认为，LastPass多次出现安全事故（尤其是2022年密码库泄露），任何在那之后仍选用LastPass的公司都难以获得同情；woadwarrior01用"First0wned"讽刺其屡次被入侵。

• **质疑数据共享必要性**：bradley13和felooboolooomba质问LastPass为何将客户数据交给Klue，认为至少应做匿名化处理。

• **推荐本地/离线密码管理器**：vrighter、username135、bradley13等强烈推荐KeePass系离线工具，认为在线密码管理器本身就是风险；MetroWind直言无法理解为何要把密码存在别人的服务器上。

• **推荐其他在线替代品**：giancarlostoro推荐Bitwarden，hbn推荐Enpass（数据存于用户自己的云存储，无集中数据库），fusslo则采用"忘记密码+临时重置"策略规避风险。

补充讨论：此次攻击实为供应链事件，除LastPass外，Gong、HackerOne、Snyk等多家知名公司也受波及；争议焦点在于——这究竟是LastPass自身问题，还是整个行业使用第三方销售工具的普遍风险？

data.author: dewey
data.article_summary:
**Arma: Cold War Assault 引擎源码开源**

Bohemia Interactive 正式开源了《武装突袭：冷战危机》（原名《闪点行动》，2001年发布）的引擎及游戏源码，代号 Poseidon。代码已现代化为 C++20，使用 CMake 和 Clang 构建，支持 Windows x64 和 Linux x64。

**三点需区分：**
- **源码**：基于 GPL-3.0 开源，可自由使用、修改和再发布
- **品牌商标**："ARMA"、"Operation Flashpoint" 等名称不随源码授权，派生项目必须改名
- **游戏资产**：模型、贴图、音频等不在此仓库，单独以 APL-SA 协议发布，Steam 提供免费 Demo

这是对二十多年来支持该游戏的社区的回馈。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bohemia Interactive 开源《冷战突击》（原《武装突袭：冷战危机》）代码及其历史影响

不同观点：
• **技术与历史意义**（murdockq）：引擎代码比当年更整洁，2001年就实现了12.5×12.5km开放世界+SQF运行时脚本，比半条命2早三年，技术上远超时代。DayZ的不稳定性也源于此引擎被过度延伸使用。

• **开源行为本身值得称赞**（klaussilveira、fishgoesblub）：BI不仅开源，还清理代码并移植到x64 Windows/Linux，非常难得；希望更多工作室效仿并采用GPL3.0协议。

• **游戏情怀与个人回忆**（fdgfgfvffdv、zuzululu、romandr、dvratil）：多位玩家分享童年/青年时期游玩经历，认为这是系列最佳作品，甚至有人因编写任务简报而学会HTML，走上开发者职业道路。

• **与现代游戏的比较**（jefc1111）：尽管操作"粗糙"，ARMA 3的沉浸感仍胜过《现代战争》《战地》等主流游戏，关键在于团队协作和通信的深度玩法。

• **开源的社区价值**（junaru）：此举与"停止毁灭游戏"运动理念契合，官方资产包可供社区学习和MOD制作，是对玩家社区的最大化授权。

补充讨论：有评论提到游戏曾有有趣的反盗版机制（破解版会让准星越来越偏）；另有WASM移植版本链接被分享，说明社区对其技术现代化也有积极行动。

data.title: Stealing Is a Skill
data.author: bewal416
data.article_summary:
这篇文章的核心观点是：**"偷窃"是一种创造力技能**。

作者借鉴设计师 Virgil Abloh 的"3%法则"——只改动原作的3%——提倡在创作初期直接复刻你欣赏的作品（像素级还原），通过彻底拆解原作的每一个细节来深度理解它。

作者与同事重建了 Mintlify 的营销网站，在逐步复刻的过程中，自然发现了属于自己品牌的那"3%"差异，最终这3%演变成了50%的原创内容。

核心结论：**创意不在于凭空原创，而在于高效识别并解决问题**。先找到"巨人的肩膀"，深入学习其100%，再有意识地注入自己的判断，这比从零开始更快、更有效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网页设计中"借鉴/抄袭"行为的边界与性质认定

不同观点：
• **抄袭即违规**：直接像素级复制他人商业作品是盗窃，不应美化。[sandcat_] 指出这与被邀请合作的设计师（如Virgil Abloh）有本质区别；[agilek] 质疑这种行为还能堂而皇之地写博客庆祝。

• **"临摹练习"有学习价值**：[dghlsakjg] 类比写作中的copywork练习，认为逐字复制是学习大师技法的有效途径；[dinkleberg] 也肯定像素级临摹对提升设计技能有价值——但仅限于练习目的。

• **"偷"的真正含义是内化，而非复制**：[rglover] 援引乔布斯语境，认为真正的"steal"是将核心思想融入自己的实现，而非照搬；[emaro] 和 [WaitWaitWha] 均认为像素级复制无法获得原作者的思考过程。

• **商业场景与社区传统需区分**：[erikschoster] 认为在社区中传承传统是正当的，但一旦进入商业市场，同样行为就构成盗窃。

• **借鉴须多元融合**：[dinkleberg] 建议从3个以上来源提取各自精华加以融合，单纯复制并微调是低劣做法；[darepublic] 的实践经验也印证了"借结构但自己手工实现"能带来真正的成长。

补充讨论：部分评论者（[sscaryterry]、[pseudosavant]）持较宽容态度，认为软件和创意领域本就是循环复用旧概念，"偷"的说法过重；而[meander_water] 则补充指出，是否公开承认来源、是否主动逆向学习，是区分良性借鉴与不良抄袭的重要维度。

48659165.article_content:
I’m slowly developing my own list of advice: have
a creative mindset
, embrace
radical transparency
, and write down
what makes you happy
. I’d like to add one more to the list: stealing is a skill!
Stealing is good for the soul. If done well, you will be able to build value at lightning pace and learn about yourself along the way.
But what is “stealing”? Is reading from a textbook considered stealing? Adopting an open-source library into your codebase? No- that’s not radical enough… I’m talking about
literally copying another person’s creation.
My coworker Justin taught me about “
the 3% approach
”, coined by the late creative, Virgil Abloh. When designing his version of Air Force 1s, Abloh disciplined himself to only edit 3% of the original design, so as not to dilute the original work perfected by visionaries before him.
Abloh never went into much detail beyond that, but Justin and I began to make it our own at Kibu. I love the 3% approach¹, particularly when engaging in a project unfamiliar to you. When asked to alter 3% of something, you are challenged to determine
which 3% you ought to alter
. This forces you to inspect all 100% of that thing: every stitch and seam of the original. To us, the best way to get to 3% was to
rebuild something we loved, stitch by stitch.
We had to steal to succeed.
Justin and I wanted to rebuild
our marketing site
, but we lacked a solid vision. We knew we wanted a beautiful
top-fold
and a modern, minimal component library that could be reused across pages. We came across
Mintlify’s 2025 marketing site
and fell in love: an eye-grabbing top-fold, decisive use of colors, and a “show, don’t tell” ethos revealed all we wanted to create. The fact that Mintlify and Kibu are both documentation tools (albeit
very
different definitions of the word) was an added bonus. So,
we literally rebuilt the Mintlify site, pixel-by-pixel.
When you recreate someone’s creation, you learn their story: every piece of brilliance, tradeoff, and imperfection.
Why add a hover effect here and not there? What does three consecutive black and white sections do to the mind? Oh wow, look how all components’ widths fall perfectly flush with the floating, bg-blurred navbar:
Mintlify’s site wasn’t perfect by any stretch; yet stealing it proved an efficient way to reach our goals. And as we stole, our intuitions brought us to that 3%.
Our nav popover can be more minimal. Our team is our brand- let’s put their faces on the CTA buttons. Our product is video- let’s show more video than screenshots.
These “side quests” taught us more about our brand than any 3-day workshop could have. In fact, they quickly became the main quest: decisions we’d thought trivial turned our “3%” into “50%.” Our real work lived in every picture and video we added. By then we couldn’t lean on Mintlify anymore. We had to trust our instincts to connect our product to our story. But that’s the point: the 97% approach never holds at 97%. Honest actors will always drift. Mintlify just gave us a North Star we agreed was “good”, so every drift had to earn its place against it. In under a month of weekend work, we had a site deployed in Framer².
Coming out of this project, I had a newfound perspective of stealing. While I’ve always admired certain people’s crafts, I now prioritize it in my ideation process. No matter the project, I always ask myself and my team, “has anyone done something similar before us?” There’s thousands of free blogs, podcasts, and videos on problems you’re actively solving. It’s never been easier to prompt AI with your use case and ask who’s come across this issue before you. However, it’s your job to go down the rabbit hole, learn the 100%, and sprinkle in your 3%.
At the beginning of my career, I believed I’d be rewarded for the originality of my ideas. The truth is that you’re rewarded for identifying and solving problems efficiently. And odds are, smarter people before you have already done both. So, turn stealing into a skill: spend your days identifying
what
you ought to steal,
why
you ought to steal it, and
how much
you’ll steal of it.
“Creativity is just connecting things. When you ask creative people how they did something, they feel a little guilty because they didn’t really do it, they just saw something.” - Steve Jobs
Blech. So cliche to end on a Jobs quote. One more:
Everything I do references something that influenced me.” - Virgil Abloh
¹ Abloh’s “3% approach” is an
approach
, not a
rule
. If you Google this term, you’ll find a lot of blogs fetishizing this as a sacred
rule
. I’d guess Abloh himself would dissuade you from that line of thinking. Abloh developed this concept in context to his work in a new Air Force 1 series: the fundamental task to mimic an existing design- a distinguished design that I’m sure Abloh heavily revered. You are allowed to be original! There is a spectrum to creative originality. This post is about one end of the spectrum.

data.title: Hightouch (YC S19) Is Hiring
data.author: joshwget
data.article_summary:

data.title: A C++ implementation of a fast hash map and hash set using hopscotch hashing
data.author: gjvc
data.article_summary:
**hopscotch-map** 是一个C++头文件库，使用开放寻址和跳房子哈希（hopscotch hashing）实现高性能哈希表，性能优于 `std::unordered_map`，内存占用少于 `google::dense_hash_map`。

主要提供四类容器：
- `tsl::hopscotch_map/set`：默认选择，速度更快，使用2的幂次增长策略
- `tsl::hopscotch_pg_map/set`：质数增长策略，适合哈希函数质量较差的场景
- `tsl::bhopscotch_map/set`：提供 O(log n) 最坏情况保证，可抵御哈希DoS攻击

核心特性包括：仅需包含头文件、支持移动语义和异类查找（heterogeneous lookup）、可缓存哈希值加速查找、可禁用异常。

与 `std::unordered_map` 的主要差异：迭代器在插入时全部失效；修改值需调用 `it.value()` 而非 `it->second`。

A C++ implementation of a fast hash map and hash set using hopscotch hashing
The hopscotch-map library is a C++ implementation of a fast hash map and hash set using open-addressing and hopscotch hashing to resolve collisions. It is a cache-friendly data structure offering better performances than
std::unordered_map
in most cases and is closely similar to
google::dense_hash_map
while using less memory and providing more functionalities.
The library provides the following main classes:
tsl::hopscotch_map
,
tsl::hopscotch_set
,
tsl::hopscotch_pg_map
and
tsl::hopscotch_pg_set
. The first two are faster and use a power of two growth policy, the last two use a prime growth policy instead and are able to cope better with a poor hash function. Use the prime version if there is a chance of repeating patterns in the lower bits of your hash (e.g. you are storing pointers with an identity hash function). See
GrowthPolicy
for details.
In addition to these classes the library also provides
tsl::bhopscotch_map
,
tsl::bhopscotch_set
,
tsl::bhopscotch_pg_map
and
tsl::bhopscotch_pg_set
. These classes have an additional requirement for the key, it must be
LessThanComparable
, but they provide a better asymptotic upper bound, see
details
in example. Nonetheless if you don't have specific requirements (risk of hash DoS attacks),
tsl::hopscotch_map
and
tsl::hopscotch_set
should be sufficient in most cases and should be your default pick as they perform better in general.
An overview of hopscotch hashing and some implementation details can be found
here
.
A
benchmark
of
tsl::hopscotch_map
against other hash maps may be found
here
. This page also gives some advices on which hash table structure you should try for your use case (useful if you are a bit lost with the multiple hash tables implementations in the
tsl
namespace).
Key features
Header-only library, just add the
include
directory to your include path and you are ready to go. If you use CMake, you can also use the
tsl::hopscotch_map
exported target from the
CMakeLists.txt
.
Fast hash table, see
benchmark
for some numbers.
Support for move-only and non-default constructible key/value.
Support for heterogeneous lookups allowing the usage of
find
with a type different than
Key
(e.g. if you have a map that uses
std::unique_ptr<foo>
as key, you can use a
foo*
or a
std::uintptr_t
as key parameter to
find
without constructing a
std::unique_ptr<foo>
, see
example
).
No need to reserve any sentinel value from the keys.
Possibility to store the hash value on insert for faster rehash and lookup if the hash or the key equal functions are expensive to compute (see the
StoreHash
template parameter).
If the hash is known before a lookup, it is possible to pass it as parameter to speed-up the lookup (see
precalculated_hash
parameter in
API
).
The
tsl::bhopscotch_map
and
tsl::bhopscotch_set
provide a worst-case of O(log n) on lookups and deletions making these classes resistant to hash table Deny of Service (DoS) attacks (see
details
in example).
The library can be used with exceptions disabled (through
-fno-exceptions
option on Clang and GCC, without an
/EH
option on MSVC or simply by defining
TSL_NO_EXCEPTIONS
).
std::terminate
is used in replacement of the
throw
instruction when exceptions are disabled.
API closely similar to
std::unordered_map
and
std::unordered_set
.
Differences compared to
std::unordered_map
tsl::hopscotch_map
tries to have an interface similar to
std::unordered_map
, but some differences exist.
Iterator invalidation on insert doesn't behave in the same way. In general any operation modifying the hash table, except
erase
, invalidate all the iterators (see
API
for details).
References and pointers to keys or values in the map are invalidated in the same way as iterators to these keys-values on insert.
For iterators,
operator*()
and
operator->()
return a reference and a pointer to
const std::pair<Key, T>
instead of
std::pair<const Key, T>
, making the value
T
not modifiable. To modify the value you have to call the
value()
method of the iterator to get a mutable reference. Example:
tsl::hopscotch_map<
int
,
int
> map = {{
1
,
1
}, {
2
,
1
}, {
3
,
1
}};
for
(
auto
it = map.begin(); it != map.end(); ++it) {
//
it->second = 2; // Illegal
it.
value
() =
2
;
//
Ok
}

data.title: The gap between open weights LLMs and closed source LLMs
data.author: kkm
data.article_summary:
本文分析了开源与闭源大语言模型（LLM）之间的能力差距。

**核心发现：**

- 若仅看"人工分析智能指数"这一单一基准，开源模型与闭源模型的差距自2024年夏开始持续缩小，按趋势推算将于**2026年12月**追平。

- 但将分析扩展至全部18个基准后，结论截然不同：整体差距几乎持平，始终维持在约**5个月**左右，并无明显收窄趋势。

- 差距缩小主要集中在**编程类基准**（从落后15个月缩短至约1-2个月），其他大多数基准的差距甚至略有扩大。

**结论：** 如何衡量LLM能力至关重要。单一基准可能得出"开源即将追平"的戏剧性结论，而多基准综合分析则显示开源模型仍稳定落后约5个月。这揭示了LLM评测本身的复杂性与局限性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源/开放权重模型的未来前景与局限性

不同观点：
• **可持续性风险**（profsummergig）：开放权重模型目前依赖私人机构（如 DeepSeek）的慈善行为，随时可能停止供应。真正的可持续需要"社区拥有的硬件"，否则模型始终面临被中断的风险。

• **蒸馏依赖悖论**（jacobgold & jackconsidine）：开放权重模型的进步在很大程度上依赖对闭源模型的"蒸馏"。jackconsidine 用芝诺悖论类比——若闭源模型停止进步，开放模型是否也会随之停滞？这与经典悖论不同：开放模型可能真的永远追不上，因为其进步本身依赖于被追赶的对象。

• **概念混淆问题**（samat）：文章将"开源模型"与"开放权重模型"混为一谈，两者并不相同。标题具有误导性，尽管正文有所区分。

补充讨论：三个观点实际上指向同一核心隐忧——开放模型在技术上（依赖蒸馏）、资源上（依赖私人资助）、概念上（定义不清晰）均缺乏真正的独立性，其"开放"的长期可信度值得质疑。

48692058.article_content:
Interactive plot of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index for open and closed frontier models.
I have seen a version of the above plot going around Twitter and wanted to dig a bit deeper into it.
What the plot above is showing is the gap between open weights LLMs and closed source LLMs.
We measure this gap by looking at the frontier of performance of open weights LLMs on a benchmark and then looking back into the past how long ago was the closed source frontier at that level.
It is a measure of how long it took for open source models to catch up to the new capabilities reached by the closed source model frontier.
This benchmark is the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - their headline index that tries to assess the overall capabilities of models.
In general it correlates quite well with the ‘vibe’ people seem to get from models.
You can see that around summer 2024 the gap on this benchmark starts to shrink, and has been reliably shrinking since then.
If you plot a line of best fit and extend it into the future you find that the gap shrinks to 0 months around
December 3rd 2026
- 6 months or so from the time of writing.
Now is probably a good time to liquidate your pension, fly to a remote island somewhere, and live out the remaining 6 months or so of civilization in peace.
…
Except.
This might not be the whole picture. This is only a single benchmark, and doesn’t give a complete picture of the capabilities of LLMs.
Kindly, Artificial Analysis gives us access to 18 different benchmarks that they have measured for these models.
I have repeated the analysis for all the 18 different benchmarks and I have summarized them in the plot below:
Interactive boxplot of monthly open frontier lag across Artificial Analysis metrics.
For each of the 18 datasets we have created a similar chart. You can see all 18 at the bottom of the page.
At each month we have created a box plot of the gap for each dataset. We have then plotted all the box plots over time.
We have also calculated the average of the gaps across datasets, and calcuated a line of best fit for that.
That line is almost completely flat, at just under 5 months for the entire period.
What is notable is that a large amount of the total improvement of models has been in the coding benchmark.
The coding index has gone from 15 months behind to only a month or two behind.
Most other datasets have a moderate increase over time in their gaps.
So maybe the open source apocalypse won’t happen yet.
What this exercise does suggest is the difficulty of measuring LLM quality. Depending on how you measure it you would predict the open source singularity by Christmas, or you would say that open source LLMs are consistently 5 months behind close source, and that the gap might be growing.

data.title: Show HN: Autofit2 – End-to-end pipeline for multilingual text classification
data.author: leschak
data.article_summary:
**autofit2** 是一个基于 SetFit 和 SBERT 嵌入的少样本文本分类框架，具备以下核心特点：

- **少样本高精度**：仅需数十个标注样本即可达到 95–99% 的分类精度。
- **多语言支持**：支持 20 种语言的预训练模型，评估语料覆盖 50+ 语言，可扩展至 100+ 种。
- **全自动流水线**：通过单一 JSON 配置文件完成数据预处理、微调、评估和部署，支持断点续训。
- **可复现性**：JSON 驱动配置，自动生成模型卡片并追踪 CO₂ 排放。

配置文件定义任务、语言、基础模型及目标类型（`all` 生成完整制品，`custom` 自定义模型，`benchmark` 仅输出评分日志）。数据加载通过 loader 命令列表注入，支持灵活的训练/测试拆分逻辑。

- **AOHell** — the hacked AOL client used to troll chatrooms and phreap free hours
- **28.8 kbps modem** — screaming its handshake into the void, tying up the phone line

data.author: speckx
data.article_summary:
英国BBC长波（LW）广播服务即将关闭。位于伍斯特郡德罗伊特威奇的两座213米高的Wychbold发射塔自1934年起服役，不仅覆盖全英广播，二战期间还用于干扰德国空军雷达、向法国抵抗组织传递秘密信息，并参与了诺曼底登陆的通讯协调。

关闭原因是设备老化，且长波听众大幅减少，多数人已转向FM和DAB数字平台，BBC认为升级设备不具成本效益。

目前，当地历史学者和"二十世纪学会"正呼吁为这两座铁塔申请历史保护建筑资格，但历史英格兰机构2025年认为其不符合标准。德罗伊特威奇遗产中心设有专题展览"德罗伊特威奇呼叫"，保存相关历史。

Long Wave radio era set to end with switch-off

Lindsey Alder
Droitwich
BBC
Local history expert Alastair Moseley said he backed a campaign to get the Wychbold masts listed status
A campaign has begun to get two large transmitter masts listed, after the BBC's Long Wave (LW) service is turned off.
The 700ft (213m) high Wychbold Masts in the Worcestershire countryside can be seen for miles and are often used as a landmark for drivers on the M5 near Droitwich.
They have been in use since 1934 for sending the signal across the country, as well as for transmitting important messages during the World War Two.
Local history experts and the Twentieth Century Society have called for them to become listed, due to their "historical importance".
Droitwich was picked as a central location for the station and masts so Long Wave could reach everywhere in the UK.
Droitwich was picked as a central location for the station and masts so Long Wave could reach everywhere in the UK
The construction was a big operation for the time and local expert Alastair Moseley, from the Bromsgrove Society, said a huge team of workers had to come and put them up
"It cost £200,000 to build then, that's about £20m now, which actually is quite a good value I think," he said.
"But the towers themselves were built by just 10 riggers and there was one particular guy, Derek Pigeon,  who actually had just come over from building Sydney's Harbour Bridge."
The main building of Droitwich Transmitting Station, which has now been demolished.
On the 6 September 1934 everything was ready to go, and the first thing the country heard on LW was a musical piece by composer Eric Coates, famed for the Dam Busters theme, called The Merry Makers.
A few years later, when World War Two started, the masts had a new job to do as Moseley explained.
"They were used to block transmissions and radar facilities from the Luftwaffe, so that they were almost blind when they were coming in to fly," he said.
"They also transmitted messages to the French Resistance, they had a part in that so it was very covert.
"And D-Day, they were part of the co-ordination of communications that were needed to make that such a successful landmark event in history".
Archive photos show what the inside of the main transmission building looked like
After the war, the transmitting station returned to its usual broadcasts.
In 1957 officials held an open day but public interest was so high that 13,000 people turned up to take a look.
That led to other transmitting stations across the country having their own open days, particularly those with new TV masts.
Droitwich Spa Heritage Centre
Thousands of people came to an open day at the Droitwich Transmitting Station in 1957
Over the years, the equipment was changed from analogue to digital and several other smaller masts were built for the Medium Wave signal.
The Wychbold Masts will no longer transmit LW with the switch-off expected at 00:01 BST on Saturday.
A spokesperson for the BBC said the move came as the equipment was reaching the end of its life.
"As Long Wave is an older broadcasting technology, recent years have seen a decline in listener numbers, with the majority now opting for FM and DAB digital platforms," they said.
"Given these factors, investing in upgrading the LW equipment is not considered a cost-effective solution for licence fee-funded services".
Original transmitting station equipment is on display in Droitwich town centre
The transmitting station's history is captured in a special exhibition in the town's heritage centre, called Droitwich Calling.
Old equipment and photos were donated by former BBC engineer John Phillips, who worked there his entire career.
He wanted to make sure the masts' legacy continued and worked with the centre until he passed away.
Rebecca Butler helped put together the Droitwich Calling exhibition
Manager Rebecca Butler said the exhibition was important to keep awareness of the masts' legacy alive.
"We're telling the stories of Droitwich Transmitting Station for future prosperity, we're holding onto these artefacts for the future," she said.
"There may be a time where those masts are no longer here, but for 92 years they have stood strong and I feel like it's something that we need to be proud of".
An event to remember and celebrate the history of the transmitting station is being held at the centre on Saturday from 12:00-16:00.
The Wychbold Masts can be seen for miles across the Worcestershire countryside
Historic England did consult on potentially listing the site in 2025 - but ultimately decided they did not meet the criteria, mainly because so much of the original buildings were demolished.
Granting a building listed status
gives it special protection.
The Twentieth Century Society, who campaign to save "outstanding buildings" from the century, want the masts themselves to be specifically considered.

data.title: PlayStation Is Deleting 551 Movies from Customers' Accounts
data.author: ortusdux
data.article_summary:
索尼将从2026年9月1日起，删除PlayStation Store用户此前购买的551部StudioCanal旗下电影和电视剧，包括《终结者2》《全面回忆》等经典作品。索尼在通知中毫无歉意地表示这是"内容授权协议"所致，既未提供退款，也无任何补偿。

此事再次揭示了数字内容购买的本质：用户点击同意服务条款时，实际上只是在"租用"内容，平台随时可以收回，用户对此毫无控制权。这也解释了为何玩家对实体游戏碟消失等数字化趋势如此敏感——数字内容从来都不真正属于消费者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数字内容平台（如索尼）单方面下架已购内容的行为是否合法，以及"购买"与"租赁"的本质区别。

不同观点：
• **盗版有理论**（thomasmarton）：购买实体DVD即拥有所有权，数字购买应享有同等权利；平台重新定义"购买"的行为值得被监管机构（如欧盟）重罚。

• **法律用词应规范**（dc3k）：产品页面标注"购买/buy"却实为限期租用，本身就是一种欺骗，应当被禁止。

• **此事并非首次**（Karliss）：索尼此前已有前科，并附上了相关历史记录链接，暗示这是企业惯常行为。

• **法律维权可行**（jmclnx）：建议用户诉诸小额法庭，亚马逊曾因类似行为被追责；同时理解为何有人选择"扬帆出海"（盗版）。

补充讨论：评论整体情绪偏向消费者权益保护，对平台行为持批评态度。争议焦点在于：**数字内容的"购买"是否等同于所有权**，以及平台是否应承担相应法律责任。盗版被部分人视为对不公平商业行为的抵制手段，而非单纯的违法行为。

to say that “you will no longer be able to access your previously purchased content from Studio Canal, and it will be removed from your video library.” There’s no mention of any refunds or make-goods for the affected users. Sony simply says the films are going away “due to our content licensing agreements,” once again reaffirming the fact that you are never truly buying anything that’s digital, just temporarily renting it.
This news was brought to people’s attention by X user somatyk, who posted the notification they had received from PlayStation this week. Along with the unapologetic news that the purchased movies would be deleted from their account on September 1, the message concluded with, “Click here for a full list of affected titles that will no longer be supported. on the PlayStation website

From Dusk Till Dawn
andÂ

, all of which are included in the list of films people thought they’d bought to own, but come September 1 will find gone from their collections. What’s really peculiar about the PlayStation message is that it’s entirely unapologetic, simply stating that “purchased content” will be “deleted” as if that’s perfectly normal. We’ve contacted Sony to ask if customers can expect a refund for their deleted movies, or at least some form of compensation.
Of course, when you scroll past the endless EULAs when you first use your PlayStation, and click “Agree” the first time you load the store, you’re unwittingly agreeing that nothing you buy is really truly bought, and that it can be taken away from you at any point, and there’s nothing you can do. The same is true of your games.
This is why people
care so much
about details like
GTA 6
releasing without a disc in its physical box
, and it underlines the risk we all take every time we buy anything from any digital store. None of it actually belongs to you, and you can only access it for as long as the company you bought it from says you can.

主要讨论点：数字内容平台（如索尼）单方面下架已购内容的行为是否合法，以及"购买"与"租赁"的本质区别。

不同观点：
• **盗版有理论**（thomasmarton）：购买实体DVD即拥有所有权，数字购买应享有同等权利；平台重新定义"购买"的行为值得被监管机构（如欧盟）重罚。

• **法律用词应规范**（dc3k）：产品页面标注"购买/buy"却实为限期租用，本身就是一种欺骗，应当被禁止。

• **此事并非首次**（Karliss）：索尼此前已有前科，并附上了相关历史记录链接，暗示这是企业惯常行为。

• **法律维权可行**（jmclnx）：建议用户诉诸小额法庭，亚马逊曾因类似行为被追责；同时理解为何有人选择"扬帆出海"（盗版）。

补充讨论：评论整体情绪偏向消费者权益保护，对平台行为持批评态度。争议焦点在于：**数字内容的"购买"是否等同于所有权**，以及平台是否应承担相应法律责任。盗版被部分人视为对不公平商业行为的抵制手段，而非单纯的违法行为。

data.title: The National Parks Were Reportedly Told to Stay Silent on Deaths
data.author: LostMyLogin
data.article_summary:
美国内政部据报向国家公园服务局（NPS）员工下发内部备忘录，禁止工作人员公开通报全国435个国家公园的死亡事件及伤亡严重程度。内政部否认刻意隐瞒，称此举旨在统一事故信息发布流程。

然而，专家和前NPS官员对此表示担忧。公园护林员协会执行主任Bill Wade指出，NPS过去一贯及时、审慎地发布死亡信息，此次政策转变原因不明，可能损害公众对该机构的信任。他还强调，这类公开报告不仅提供准确信息，也起到提醒游客安全风险的重要作用。

新政策实施后，约塞米蒂公园一名23岁游客坠瀑身亡、红杉国家公园一名少女溺水等事故均未在NPS官网上得到任何记录。

专家警告，透明度降低可能直接威胁游客安全，隐瞒事故信息将使公众无法了解潜在危险，进而增加类似悲剧发生的风险。

Published June 25, 2026 04:34PM
A newly revealed internal memo allegedly bans National Park Service (NPS) staff from publicly reporting the deaths or severity of injuries at America’s national parks, according to a new report. Experts say this shift in transparency not only sets a dangerous precedent for park management but could also put visitors at risk.
According to a report recently published by
The Washington Post
, the Department of the Interior (DOI), which oversees NPS, distributed a memo to employees in December. Park staff and those who speak to the media were reportedly prohibited from notifying the public about deaths and certain injuries across 435 NPS sites nationwide.
In an email to
Outside
, a spokesperson for the DOI said the “narrative being presented is false and reflects a significant mischaracterization of the Department’s guidance.”
“Interior remains committed to providing timely and accurate information while ensuring families are notified first. The guidance was developed to create a more consistent approach to incident communications across the Department and is not intended to conceal fatalities or delay information,” the spokesperson wrote.
ADVERTISEMENT
“We continue to provide public safety information, statements, news releases, and incident updates as appropriate, while respecting investigative processes, privacy considerations, next-of-kin notifications, and, in some cases, requests from family members not to release identifying information,” they added.
However, some experts say that the shift is unnecessary and could have repercussions for park visitors.
“This is a significant change in reporting requirements, and we do not know or understand the reason or motivation for the change,” Bill Wade, executive director of the advocacy group,
Association of National Park Rangers
, told
Outside
. Wade spent 34 years working for the NPS across several sites, including Mount Rainier and Yosemite. He said the change could erode public trust in the agency and harm its reputation.
“In the past, the NPS has consistently done a good job of providing measured, incremental reports on fatalities and has not been speculative, nor provided relevant details that should not be reported until next-of-kin have been notified or investigative requirements are met,” he added.
ADVERTISEMENT
In the last week, the NPS failed to publicly report a series of deaths at areas under its jurisdiction; a 23-year-old died after
falling off a waterfall
in Yosemite, and a teenage girl
drowned in Sequoia National Park
during a hike.
Outside
found no record of either event on the
NPS website
.

The Washington Post
, the internal policy states “Interior shall not confirm a death,” and that this policy applies to “all Interior bureaus and offices” plus “all Interior communications involving fatalities, suspected fatalities, serious injuries or emotionally sensitive incidents.”
Only “appropriate authorities” can confirm a death, the outlet noted.
“Interior shall not confirm the severity of injuries,” the memo reportedly said, according to
The Washington Post
. “Interior may state only that an individual was transported and the method of transport. No additional medical information may be released.”
Staff can confirm that an incident occurred, the general location, that the department is responding, and that an investigation is ongoing; additional information will be shared when appropriate,
The Washington Post
said.
The memo further states that the new policy applies to “all Interior bureaus and offices,” the publication reported.
The Potential Dangers of Park Secrecy
Transparency can save lives, and keeping park deaths quiet may put visitors at risk.

data.title: The Art of Kite Flying (1430–1929)
data.author: benbreen
data.article_summary:
这篇文章探讨了风筝的历史与文化。

**语言与名称**：各国对风筝的称呼各异，有"纸鹰"、"龙"、"飞鹿"、"空中蛇"、"风筝"（源自竹笛）等，折射出不同文化对风筝的想象。

**起源之争**：风筝通常被认为起源于中国，传说墨子和鲁班曾制造木鸟。但也有观点认为波利尼西亚等地的风筝传统更为古老，且在这些地区风筝曾具有宗教与驱魔功能。

**娱乐与节庆**：中国约1000年前开始以风筝为娱乐，重阳节放风筝的习俗源于避祸传说。印度莫卧儿时代风筝活动盛行，古吉拉特邦的节庆中放风筝甚至曾导致大量鸟类受伤。

**军事用途**：风筝在军事上用于侦察、传递信号、心理战（如抛撒传单），也曾被用于鼓舞士气。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：风筝——从传统玩法到现代装备的演变

不同观点：
• **书籍推荐派（zabzonk）**：认为《企鹅风筝书》是最佳入门资源，涵盖历史与手工制作，强调用易得材料自制风筝的传统方式。

• **传统竞技派（samudrijan）**：分享儿时"斗风筝"经历——竹骨盾形风筝灵活好操控，线上涂抹胶水混玻璃粉用于割断对手线，被割断的风筝归捡到者所有，甚至可用尾线缠绕收回落败风筝。体现了风筝作为竞技活动的民间传统。

• **现代便利派（bethekidyouwant）**：推崇速卖通上的现代风筝产品，重点推荐自动收线绕线器解决了放线收线的烦恼；同时指出飞翼式索具设计是近年重要创新，认为这一改进本可更早实现。

补充讨论：三位用户代表了风筝文化的三个维度——知识传承（书籍）、民间竞技传统（斗风筝）、现代商业化便利产品。争议点隐含在传统手作与购买现成品之间的取向差异，以及"创新是否来得太晚"的感叹。
